targetAudience.primary: Multi-agent runtime, A2A integration and agent-security architects
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands session histories, structured tool calls and cross-agent context handoff.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A locally legitimate session event can become an unauthorized disclosure when replayed to another agent, especially after rendering erases the structure needed for filtering.

whyNow: A same-day merged Google ADK fix removes credential-bearing request calls from RemoteA2aAgent outbound history before rendering, while preserving the richer original local event and non-secret siblings.

externalHook.description: A session log can be valid local evidence and invalid remote context at the same time.

coreProposition: Cross-agent history should be a destination-specific, policy-enforcing projection of mixed-trust local state: remove unauthorized control material while its semantic structure is still available, preserve legitimate local evidence separately, and do not mistake selective projection for general confidentiality or peer trust.

originalValue.description: Reframes history reconstruction as an outbound disclosure decision, separating local evidence retention, destination authorization, representation order and transport trust.

readerTakeaway: Introduce an explicit projection stage before rendering or serialization, give sensitive control events durable semantic identity, and audit withholding without reproducing the secret.

supported: RemoteA2aAgent reconstructs outbound messages from local session history.
Credential-bearing request calls are removed before rendering can inline structured arguments into text.
The detector combines known call names with nested AuthConfig shape and preserves ordinary siblings.
Filtering uses a deep-copied outbound representation and leaves the original local event intact.
unsupported: General A2A confidentiality or remote-peer authorization
Coverage of every outbound adapter and future transformation
uncertain: How every event producer should attach durable disclosure labels
How a runtime proves all outbound adapters use the mandatory projection boundary

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article concerns general multi-agent context architecture and requires no first-party project mapping.

decisionReason: The implementation exposes a precise ordering-sensitive disclosure boundary, and the Research Object derives a broadly useful architecture without exceeding the source evidence.
